THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C.M. POONACHA
ORAL JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 18.6.2018 passed in MVC No.875/2016 by the III Additional District Judge and Additional MACT-III,
Shivamogga1 seeking enhancement of compensation.

The Tribunal by its judgment and award dated 18.6.2018 awarded a total compensation of `85,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a.
2.
The findings of the Tribunal on negligence and liability are not under challenge and have attained finality.
Hence, the only question that is required to be considered is as to 'whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is required to be enhanced?'
Hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' NC: 2025:KHC:24980 HC-KAR 3.
The claimant was aged 44 years as on the date of the accident.
It is averred in the claim petition that he was working as a driver at Sharavathi Dental College and Hospital, Shivamogga and earning a sum of `30,000/- p.m.

entities.text: Sharavathi Dental College and Hospital, Shivamogga
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The salary certificate (Ex.P11) discloses that the claimant was paid a consolidated salary of `11,546/- and after deductions towards PF and ESI of a total sum of `1,589/-,
he was paid a net salary of `9,957/-.
But, no witness has been examined to prove Ex.P11.
No other material is produced to demonstrate that the claimant was being paid the monthly salary.

Hence,
the Tribunal appreciating the material on record has noticed that PW.1 in the cross-examination has admitted that he was still working in the same institution and that he has not stated as to whether he was working as an attender or a driver.
4. The claimant sustained fracture of right hand humerus and crush injury to the 4th toe of the right leg apart from other simple injuries.
The orthopaedic surgeon (PW2) has deposed that the claimant was admitted on 25.07.2016, on which day, PW2 has conducted the surgery and the claimant was discharged on 26.07.2016.

The disability certificate (Ex.P9) and the treatment certificate (Ex.P10)

sentences.text: It is further stated in Ex.P9 that there is 100% loss of grip strength, 90% loss of pinch strength and there is 28% disability to the right upper limb functioning.
Ex . P10
discloses that the claimant was treated as an out-patient on 2.1.2017 and that follow-up treatment including hand therapy and medications was given on 13.7.2017, 24.10.2017 and 6.11.2017.
The Doctor who issued Exs.P9 and P10 was examined through a Court Commissioner as CW.1 and have reiterated the contents of Exs.P9 and P10.
Another doctor (PW.3) has deposed that claimant took treatment as an inpatient from 1.9.2016 to 9.9.2016 at Subbaiah Medical College and Hospital, Shivamogga.

sentences.text: The medical records of Subbaiah Medical College Hospital & Research Centre, Shimoga have been produced as Ex.P16 which discloses that the claimant underwent a surgery on 03.09.2016 for K-wire implant removal.

sentences.text: 5. It is forthcoming from the records that the claimant was registered under the Employees' State Insurance Corporation and hence, the medical expenses have been reimbursed.
NC: 2025:KHC:24980 HC-KAR 6.
Having regard to the aforementioned, the compensation is re
- assessed as follows:
6.1 The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities of `50,000/- and `25,000/- respectively is just and proper.

6.2 Having regard to the nature of injuries and period of treatment, the compensation towards food, nourishment and attendant charges is re-assessed as `20,000/- as against `5,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Since compensation has been awarded towards food, nourishment and attendant charges, the compensation of `5,000/- towards transportation charges awarded by the Tribunal is set aside.

6.3 Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, it is clear that the claimant would not have been able to resume his regular work immediately and some time would be required for him to recover from injuries.

Although no material is produced with regard to leave that he has taken from his employment, taking note of the income of the claimant as has been discussed at para No.3 and assessing the laid up period of NC: 2025:KHC:24980 HC-KAR two months, it is just and proper to award a sum of `20,000/-
towards loss of income.
6.4 Since the claimant has stated that he has continued in his employment, the Tribunal was justified in not awarding any compensation towards loss of future income/disability.
7. It is noticed that the Tribunal has awarded interest at 6% per annum.
However, taking judicial notice of the interest payable towards fixed deposits, it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 7% p.a., on the compensation as re-assessed by this Court.
